title: Rome grants daily venials coexist with justifying grace (Bellarmine)
source_text: XXVII. Primo enim ultro confitentur neminem in hac vita, saltem juxta legem ordinariam, absque omni peccato vivere; sed illos ipsos qui justificati sunt & justificantem gratiam conservant, obnoxios manere multis quotidianis, & levioribus peccatis; quae cum gratia justificante simul consistere possunt: nec illam statim excutiunt, quemadmodum excuti putant peccatis gravioribus, & atrocioribus, quae Apostolus carnis opera vocat. Quod ex professo probat & tuetur Bellarminus contra Pelagianos, lib. 1. de Amissione gratiae & statu peccati, cap. 5. & 6.
pass_a_gloss: For first they freely confess that no one in this life, at least according to the ordinary law, lives without all sin; but that those very ones who are justified and conserve justifying grace remain liable to many daily and lighter sins, which can coexist with justifying grace: nor do they immediately shake it off, as they think it is shaken off by graver and more atrocious sins, which the Apostle calls works of the flesh. Which Bellarmine expressly proves and defends against the Pelagians, book 1 On the Loss of Grace and the State of Sin, chapters 5 and 6.
pass_b_english: Rome admits no one ordinarily lives sinless; daily lighter sins coexist with justifying grace.
Bellarmine vs Pelagians: grace is cast off by graver flesh-works, not by those venials.
